Let
\[
m_k=\mathbb E[X^k],\qquad a=m_5,\qquad b=m_6.
\]
The fixed data are
\[
m_0=1,\quad m_1=\frac12,\quad m_2=\frac13,\quad m_3=\frac14,\quad m_4=\frac15.
\]

Since \(X\in[0,1]\), for every cubic polynomial \(q\),
\[
\mathbb E[q(X)^2]\ge 0.
\]
Thus the moment matrix
\[
\begin{pmatrix}
1&1/2&1/3&1/4\\
1/2&1/3&1/4&1/5\\
1/3&1/4&1/5&a\\
1/4&1/5&a&b
\end{pmatrix}
\]
is positive semidefinite. Taking the Schur complement of its upper-left \(3\times3\) block, whose inverse is
\[
\begin{pmatrix}
9&-36&30\\
-36&192&-180\\
30&-180&180
\end{pmatrix},
\]
gives
\[
b\ge 180a^2-57a+\frac{1857}{400}. \tag{1}
\]

Also, since \(X(1-X)\ge0\), for every quadratic \(q\),
\[
\mathbb E[X(1-X)q(X)^2]\ge0.
\]
Using the Schur complement of the upper-left \(2\times2\) block of the corresponding localizing matrix gives
\[
b\le -120a^2+43a-\frac{369}{100}. \tag{2}
\]
Combining (1) and (2),
\[
300a^2-100a+\frac{3333}{400}\le0,
\]
so
\[
\frac{33}{200}\le a\le \frac{101}{600}.
\]

Now
\[
\operatorname{Corr}(X^2,X^3)
=
\frac{a-\frac1{12}}
{\sqrt{\left(\frac15-\frac19\right)\left(b-\frac1{16}\right)}}
=
\frac{a-\frac1{12}}
{\sqrt{\frac4{45}\left(b-\frac1{16}\right)}}.
\]
For fixed \(a\), this is maximized by minimizing \(b\), so use equality in (1). Let
\[
D(a)=180a^2-57a+\frac{229}{50}.
\]
Then we maximize
\[
\frac{(a-\frac1{12})^2}{D(a)}
\]
on \(\left[\frac{33}{200},\frac{101}{600}\right]\). Its derivative has the sign of
\[
\frac{441}{100}-27a,
\]
which is negative throughout this interval, since \(\frac{33}{200}>\frac{49}{300}\). Hence the maximum occurs at
\[
a=\frac{33}{200}.
\]
Then (1) gives
\[
b=180\left(\frac{33}{200}\right)^2-57\left(\frac{33}{200}\right)+\frac{1857}{400}
=\frac{69}{500}.
\]
Therefore
\[
\max \operatorname{Corr}(X^2,X^3)
=
\frac{\frac{33}{200}-\frac1{12}}
{\sqrt{\frac4{45}\left(\frac{69}{500}-\frac1{16}\right)}}
=
\frac{\frac{49}{600}}{\frac{\sqrt{151}}{150}}
=
\boxed{\frac{49}{4\sqrt{151}}}.
\]

This value is attainable: take support
\[
0,\quad \frac{6-\sqrt6}{10},\quad \frac{6+\sqrt6}{10}
\]
with weights
\[
\frac19,\quad \frac49+\frac1{6\sqrt6},\quad \frac49-\frac1{6\sqrt6}.
\]
These weights give \(m_1=\frac12,m_2=\frac13\), and since the two nonzero support points satisfy
\[
x^3=\frac65x^2-\frac3{10}x,
\]
the recurrence verifies \(m_3=\frac14,m_4=\frac15,m_5=\frac{33}{200},m_6=\frac{69}{500}\). Thus the bound is sharp.
